The method assumes a simple random sample and a proportion outcome.

How to use this calculator

  1. Enter confidence level, margin of error, expected proportion and the remaining inputs.
  2. Select Calculate to see the answer and its breakdown.
  3. Keep a scenario, change an input and compare the results.

Use consistent units and check the assumptions below before applying the result.

How sample size is calculated

The large-population estimate is n₀=z²p(1−p)/e². For finite population N, apply n=n₀/[1+(n₀−1)/N]. The method assumes a simple random sample and a proportion outcome. At 95% confidence, 5% margin, and p=0.5, a large population needs about 385 responses.

n₀=z²p(1−p)/e²; finite population n=n₀/[1+(n₀−1)/N].
A worked example

At 95% confidence, 5% margin, and p=0.5, a large population needs about 385 responses.

Assumptions & useful context

The result depends on the values you enter and the method described above. Displayed numbers may be rounded; calculations use the unrounded values. Check that this model matches your situation before relying on it.

Frequently asked questions

Why is 50% the default proportion?

It maximizes p(1−p), producing a conservative largest sample estimate when the true share is unknown.

Does this guarantee a representative sample?

No; nonresponse and sampling design can introduce bias that the formula does not remove.
